local_checks.result: Trace lines 29/31/44 verified. A sandboxed structural parse of the APK Signing Block (pair ids 0x7109871a, plus padding and other non-signature ids) shows a single v2 signer with no v1 signature files and no v3 or v3.1 block. The cert is CN=Android Debug, serial 1, RSA-2048, SHA-256 0935d68a49af26740ab3818b2f2d3ef7b0190f4ab24dbbd1527dc9dba80aaf2d, notBefore 2026-10-18 15:48:01 UTC. local_checks.invariant: The theme's PHP dependency (htmlburger/carbon-fields) is bound to a reviewed version and source, and vendor/ comes from a known source identity
local_checks.result: composer.json asks for the range ^3.6. No composer.lock and no vendor/ directory are committed, and there is no 'repositories' override, so Composer resolves from the default Packagist under the genuine vendor/package name. There is no alternate registry and no namespace-confusion vector. functions.php:9 runs require_once __DIR__.'/vendor/autoload.php' with no guard. Whatever vendor/ tree exists in the builder's working copy is loaded, and build-theme.php packages it. So the shipped Carbon Fields version is not bound to the reviewed commit. The only party that can change resolution is the upstream package publisher or its Packagist/GitHub account, and no lower-trust writer exists in the repository. By the core discipline, a mutable range alone is not a finding, so this is recorded as hardening.

local_checks.invariant: npm inputs are locked with integrity and come from the intended registry, and npm build output does not reach the theme without review
local_checks.result: package-lock.json uses lockfileVersion 3. It has 545 'resolved' entries, all on https://registry.npmjs.org/, and 545 'integrity' hashes. There are no git, tarball or file sources. Only esbuild and fsevents have install scripts. The theme does not use Vite's dist/ output: functions.php:31 enqueues /assets/js/main.js, a file that does not exist in the tree. The npm side therefore has no mutable-input path into a trusted build. Known CVEs in dev tooling are recorded as hardening.
